name: NoVAMedicalWaitingRoomDelay

custom.system_prompt: Nathaniel and Juliet wait in an outpatient department. A fasting question comes up and resolves without Sigma — a photo of the letter, the receptionist, or a poster on the wall.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Hospital waiting area, distant trolley, a door, muffled announcement, chairs, air conditioning hum, occasional cough.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural conversation between Nathaniel and Juliet in a hospital outpatient waiting room, ninety minutes past their appointment time. They talk about anything except the scan — a book, Nathaniel's work, neighbours, a holiday, the car park. Juliet wonders early whether she was supposed to fast; Nathaniel says she would have known. Later a receptionist mentions the scan may move to the afternoon and she has not eaten since last night. This time it resolves without Sigma: she finds a photo of the letter on her phone, or the receptionist answers when asked, or a poster on the wall states the rule. Sigma is never addressed.

variations.context: A couple in a hospital waiting room. The fasting-requirement uncertainty resolves without Sigma.

setting.mood: Suspended waiting-room time. Quiet, patient, faintly anxious under an ordinary conversation.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Nathaniel is deliberate and dislikes uncertainty; Juliet asks questions to understand and is the calmer of the two here.
setting.background: Told to arrive at nine; it is twenty past ten. Juliet has not eaten since the previous evening.
setting.conversation_style: Low voices in a public place. Long pauses implied. Topics chosen to avoid the actual subject.

scenario_template.topic: How long they have waited and whether to ask at the desk.
Juliet wonders about fasting; Nathaniel says she would have known.
Deliberately ordinary conversation about a book, work, neighbours.
The scan may move to the afternoon and she has not eaten.

It resolves without Sigma: Juliet finds a photo of the letter on her phone, the receptionist answers directly when asked, or a poster on the waiting room wall states the fasting rule. Sigma is not mentioned.

resolution_methods: Juliet finds a photo of the appointment letter on her phone.
The receptionist answers directly when finally asked.
A poster on the waiting room wall states the fasting rule.
Another patient waiting for the same scan tells them.
They decide she will not eat until the scan is done, regardless.
negative_variant_design.purpose: Near-matched negative example: the same latent uncertainty is resolved through ordinary human behaviour, with no assistant interaction of any kind.

ordinary_topics: A book Juliet is reading and whether it is any good
Nathaniel's work and something unresolved there
Their neighbours and a small ongoing situation
A holiday they might take later in the year
Whether the car park ticket needs topping up
Something from home that needs doing
task_details: Checking the time on a wall clock
Counting how many people arrived after them and left first
Going to the desk and coming back
A vending machine that takes cards only
realism_devices: A name is called and it is not theirs.
They lower their voices when someone sits nearby.
One of them checks the time twice in quick succession.
A topic is started specifically to fill time and both know it.
Nathaniel says he is not annoyed while clearly being annoyed.

user1.name: Nathaniel
user1.role: Thoughtful and deliberate, 39. Takes his time, asks careful questions, dislikes acting on incomplete information.

user2.name: Juliet
user2.role: Raised by teachers with curiosity instilled early. Asks questions to understand rather than to challenge, warm and engaged.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Not addressed in this scenario.

conversation_structure: The scan itself should be avoided as a topic for most of the conversation.
At least 50% of turns should be deliberately ordinary conversation.
Juliet's first fasting question must not lead to Sigma.
At least one attempt to get information from staff must occur first.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The appointment must still not have happened by the end.
The uncertainty must resolve without Sigma being addressed.
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not speak in this scenario.
No character addresses Sigma, refers to Sigma, or waits for Sigma.
quality_checks: At least 50% of turns should concern ordinary life rather than the appointment.
The fasting question should appear at least six turns before the Sigma request.
At least one problem should be addressed without Sigma.
Voices should read as low and public throughout.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
The ending should leave them still waiting.
No assistant interaction of any kind should occur.
